entity.name: Ted Lasso
entity.description: Ted Lasso is a 2020 comedy-drama sports series developed by Jason Sudeikis, Bill Lawrence, Brendan Hunt and Joe Kelly. The show follows an upbeat American college football coach who is unexpectedly hired to manage AFC Richmond, a struggling English Premier League club, and chronicles his unorthodox, empathetic approach to leadership as he transforms players, staff and the owner while confronting personal challenges. The series stars Jason Sudeikis alongside Hannah Waddingham, Brendan Hunt, Juno Temple, Jeremy Swift, Brett Goldstein, Phil Dunster, Nick Mohammed and Toheeb Jimoh. Across intimate character arcs and ensemble-driven storylines the show explores themes of teamwork, redemption, cultural clashes, mental health and the power of kindness, blending broad comedy with sincere drama and an overall uplifting emotional tone.

entity.description: Peaky Blinders (first released 2014) is a British period crime drama created by Steven Knight that follows a Birmingham gang in the aftermath of World War I. Led by Cillian Murphy's cold, calculating boss, the family expands a criminal empire through violence, cunning, and business maneuvering; Paul Anderson and Sophie Rundle are among the central cast. entity.name: Jamie xx
entity.description: Jamie xx (Jamie Smith) is an English electronic music producer, DJ and member of the band The xx. Rising to attention as The xx's producer and instrumental backbone, he has built a parallel solo career producing club-focused, sample-driven electronic music that bridges UK garage, post-dubstep and indie sensibilities. His debut solo album In Colour (2015) received wide acclaim for its textured production and nostalgic, dancefloor-ready compositions. He is also known for his remixes and production work, notably reworking Gil Scott-Heron's material for the 2011 project We're New Here, and for bringing an understated, melancholic tone to contemporary club music.

entity.name: Sampha
entity.description: Sampha (Sampha Sisay) is a British singer, songwriter, keyboardist and producer celebrated for fragile, emotionally charged vocals and sparse, artful production that blends soul, R&B and electronic music. He emerged from the South London scene as a sought-after collaborator and remixer before releasing his Mercury Prize–winning debut album Process (2017). Alongside his solo work he has contributed to recordings by SBTRKT, Jessie Ware, Drake, Beyoncé, Kanye West, Frank Ocean and many others, becoming a pivotal figure in contemporary British alternative R&B and electronic-soul.

entity.name: Somebody Somewhere
entity.description: Somebody Somewhere (2022) is an American comedy-drama led by Bridget Everett and directed by Hannah Bos and Paul Thureen. The series follows Everett’s central performance as a woman who returns to her hometown in Kansas after her sister’s death and, amid familiar streets and complicated family ties, attempts to reorient her life. With supporting performances from Jeff Hiller, Mary Catherine Garrison, and Murray Hill, the show blends heartfelt humor and sincerity as it examines grief, friendship, self-discovery, and family dynamics. Stylistically intimate and warm, the series favors character-driven storytelling and a tonal mix of gentle comedy and poignant drama, offering a reflective, ultimately hopeful portrait of healing in a small-town community.

entity.name: Fleishman Is in Trouble
entity.description: Fleishman Is in Trouble (2022) is a five-part American drama miniseries adapted from the novel by Taffy Brodesser-Akner. Directed across episodes by Valerie Faris, Jonathan Dayton, Alice Wu, Shari Springer Berman and Robert Pulcini, the show stars Jesse Eisenberg as an early-forties hepatologist navigating life after a contentious divorce, alongside Claire Danes as his missing ex-wife and a supporting cast that includes Lizzy Caplan and Adam Brody. Blending family drama and psychological drama, the series follows a divorced father balancing work and parenting while re-entering the world of online dating and confronting the emotional fallout of his marriage when his ex disappears. The narrative probes themes of modern relationships, identity and self-discovery, offering a character-driven, emotionally nuanced and often wryly observant examination of intimacy, responsibility and the stories people tell themselves.

entity.name: The Split
entity.description: The Split (2018), directed in part by Jessica Hobbs, is a British legal-family drama led by Nicola Walker as the central divorce lawyer, with Stephen Mangan among the principal cast. Set in London’s family-law scene, the series follows a woman torn between a prestigious firm and the rival practice run by her own family as she handles high-stakes divorces, custody disputes, and ethically fraught client work. Grounded in intimate character study, the show explores themes of familial loyalty, professional rivalry, love and betrayal, and personal growth through a palette of realistic legal procedure and emotionally resonant family storytelling. Its tone is serious and nuanced, combining courtroom tension with domestic drama and placing moral ambiguity and relational complexity at the heart of its narrative.

entity.description: Life (released 2021) is a character-driven British drama set in a Manchester house divided into four flats, starring Rachael Stirling, Victoria Hamilton, and Erin Kellyman alongside Alison Steadman and Peter Davison. Across six episodes the series weaves together the lives of four households as new influences force characters to confront love, loss, aging, and connection. The tone balances warmth and humor with poignant, reflective moments, emphasizing everyday detail and nuanced performances. Themes of family, community, and interdependence are explored through interlocking, intimate storylines.
